summary: Verification: WebFetch was NOT blocked for most provider domains this run, so 40 of the 45 sampled slugs were confirmed live by directly reading their own pages; no shutdown, acquisition, or availability changes were found. 4 slugs (inmotion-hosting, akamai-functions, azure-playfab, oracle-cloud) returned 403/404 or only a redirect stub and are omitted from checked_active. packetframe's page loaded but showed an 'Under Construction' banner, a 2024 copyright, and a broken contact email -- ambiguous staleness, not shutdown evidence, so no alert was raised and it was left out of checked_active too; worth a manual look. Northflank's homepage and BYOC page both carry a banner disclosing a recent security incident and asking users to rotate credentials; that's a security advisory, not a status/availability change, so no status_alert was raised, but it's flagged here for attention. Discovery: one new candidate, OpenRelay (openrelay.inc), a YC S26 on-demand GPU cloud (formerly VectorLay), verified on its own site with live pricing; confidence kept low as a very new, small company. AGBCLOUD and CoreWeave Sandboxes leads could not be confirmed first-party (agb.cloud did not resolve; coreweave.com/products/sandboxes 404'd), so neither is proposed. No updates or status_alerts: the material facts found (AWS App Runner sunset, Flightcontrol/Ravion transition) were already correctly reflected in the existing catalog.

new_candidates.name: OpenRelay
new_candidates.summary: On-demand GPU cloud (formerly VectorLay, Y Combinator S26) offering hourly-billed GPU VMs and an OpenAI-compatible inference gateway, with a published per-GPU pricing table from RTX 3090 up to B300.
new_candidates.best_for: Developers wanting quick, no-commitment access to a range of GPU types for inference or training without reservations or quotas.
new_candidates.change_note: New GPU cloud provider not yet in the inventory; verified directly on its official site, which lists live pricing, VM deployment, and an OpenAI-compatible inference gateway.
